description: Contract cases for the field controller's REST API v1 (controller/atalaia_controller/api.py; the Android controller, app/lib/controller/controller_api.dart, decision PE24). Each case starts a fresh controller (no games, node id 0, a radio that is up, a clock at 0) and runs its steps in order. A 'request' step sends method and path with the token named (gm, read, none: no Authorization header, bad: an unknown token) and the JSON body if given; the answer must have the status and, if given, a body matching 'json'. 'save' keeps values of the answer (dotted paths) under names; '${name}' in a path or as a whole string value stands for a saved value. An 'rx' step is a decrypted packet from a box as the radio gives it (HELLO, STATE: the payload's fields by name, counters by team id; EVENT: the event, encoded by the core's codec, prio from the schema when not given). An 'advance_ms' step moves the controller's clock on and runs its tick once. Stream steps (WS /api/v1/stream, added with slice S2 of PE24): 'ws_connect' opens a connection under a name with the token named ('via': 'query', the default, puts it in ?token=, 'header' in Authorization), and the first message must match 'hello', or, with 'close', the controller must close it with that code before any message; 'ws' takes every message that connection got since its last 'ws' step (the runner publishes a marker {'type': 'pong', 'sentinel': n} through the stream after them and drops the markers), and they must match 'messages' as a list, so nothing may come in between or be missing; 'ws_send' sends 'json' and the next message must match 'reply'; 'ws_flood' hands 'count' messages {'type': 'system', 'kind': 'test', 'i': i} to every open connection at once, before any is sent, and the controller must close the connection named with code 'close' (a client more than 'stream_max_queue' messages behind, a case setting: 256 when not given). An 'mqtt' step takes every message the controller published to its MQTT broker since the last 'mqtt' step, as {'topic', 'qos', 'retain', 'payload' (the JSON payload)}, and they must match the list given. 'mqtt_acl' lists who may read and write which topics. A 'restart' step (added with slice S3) stops the controller and starts a new one on the same store, as after a reboot or a crash: the clock goes on, the open stream connections end (a 'ws_connect' after it opens one to the new controller), the MQTT messages go on to the same list. A case may set 'persist_game_key' (true when not given: decision OT-7), the controller's setting for the whole case, before and after its restarts. Radio steps (added with slice S4): an 'rx' step may set 'ack': true (the packet asks for an ACK); 'tx' takes everything the controller asked of its radio since the last 'tx' step, in order, and it must match the list given ('kinds' keeps only those kinds): a packet is {'kind': its message type (HELLO, EVENT, ACK, STATE, CMD, TIME...), 'source', 'seq', 'hop_limit', 'prio' (telemetry, normal, critical), 'ack' (an ACK requested), 'fields': the payload by the field names of protocol/schema/messages.yaml, bytes in hex}; the modem's commands are {'kind': 'configure', 'game_id', 'node_id', 'epoch', 'max_hops', 'channel_hz'} (the key is never shown), {'kind': 'clear'}, {'kind': 'channel', 'channel_hz'} and {'kind': 'peer_epochs', 'epochs': {node id: epoch}}. 'radio_state' ('up' or 'down') is the modem's link going down or coming back; 'tx_ack' {'seq', 'status'} is the modem's TX_ACK. Joins (slice S4): a case may set 'join_key' (the field join key, hex; none when not given: joins are refused with 503); a 'join_decode' step opens the join text given (usually a saved one) with it and its fields (protocol/join.md's names, bytes in hex) must match 'json'; 'save' works as for a request. Android props on Wi-Fi (WS /api/v1/prop, protocol/prop-link.md; slice S4): 'prop_connect' opens a link under a name for 'node_id' with the game key 'key' (hex, usually a saved join_decode's) to the game 'game_id' (the saved ${gid} when not given): the runner answers the challenge with the proof, and the first message must match 'welcome', or, with 'close', the messages until the controller closes it must match 'messages' and the close code 'close'; 'prop_send' sends 'json' on a link; 'prop' takes every message the link got since its last look (the runner sends a ping after them and stops at its pong), which must match 'messages'; 'prop_closed' takes the messages until the controller closes the link, which must match 'messages', and its close code 'close'. Check-in and positions (slice S5): every controller has field check-in and player positions set up, with no field CA (HTTPS off: the poster has no text), the privacy notice version 1, the portugal limit template and the default check-in settings; its wall clock starts at 'wall_start' (Unix seconds) and moves with the clock, and the field's day is in UTC. A request or 'ws_connect' step may give 'bearer', a token to send as it is (usually a saved player token, '${ptok}') instead of a named one; 'ws_closed' takes every message a connection gets until the controller closes it, which must match 'messages', and its close code 'close'. The chrono readings in the cases are signed with a fixed test key (Ed25519, seed bytes 0 to 31; its public key is the one the cases register). Matching: an object matches when every key given matches (other keys are free); '$absent' as a value means the key must not be there and '$any' that it must be there; a list matches element by element and must have the same length, except {'$contains': [...]}, where each pattern must match some element. Boxes over the radio, adoption and firmware updates (added with slice S7c, the cases named 'S7c ...'): every controller also has field cards and firmware updates set up (no USB adoption, as on a phone; firmware releases in the case's folder, trusting the case's 'firmware_keys', standard base64 public keys, none when not given), and the free boxes, invites, GAME_OVER and pairing by code when the case has a 'join_key'; a case may set 'https': true (the controller serves HTTPS: its field CA's SHA-256 is the bytes 0 to 31 and its address https://192.0.2.10:8443, join keys 13 and 14). A 'field_rx' step is a field frame a box sends (its fields: 'kind', bytes in hex, sealed with the case's join key under a nonce from that device's own counter, boot 1 and counting; with 'replay': true the previous one again), heard with RSSI -61 and SNR 7; a 'pair_rx' step a pair frame in the clear (RSSI -62, SNR 6); 'field_ack' the radio's FIELD_ACK ('id' counts the controller's field and pair frames from 1, 'status'); 'field_tx' takes the field and pair frames the controller sent since the last 'field_tx' step, decoded as {'type': 'field' or 'pair', 'kind', its fields, bytes in hex}, and they must match the list given ('kinds' keeps only those kinds, 'save' keeps values); 'pair_box' plays an unadopted box answering the last START with the 'code' it shows (REPLY with its own scalar, 32 bytes 0x6b unless 'yb' is given), 'pair_box_done' the box answering the last KEY (its confirmation must match; the opened join key and field name must match 'opened'; DONE with 'result', adopted by default, and the fingerprint of the key opened unless 'fingerprint' is given). A request may send raw bytes ('body_hex', or 'body_text' as UTF-8) instead of JSON, with 'headers', and 'mac_key' (hex) puts HMAC-SHA256 of the body with that key in X-Atalaia-Mac, as a box signs its firmware report; an answer that is not JSON is checked by 'text' (exactly) or 'bytes_sha256'. A 'tx' pattern of '$any' just takes what was sent. A 'tag_check' step (decision TW-1) takes the answer of POST /api/v1/games/{id}/tags ('payload', 'ndef', 'memory', saved with '${name}') with the 'game_id', the 'player', the 'team' id and the number of 'teams' it was asked for, and the runner checks, with its own tag code, that the NDEF record and the Type 2 memory hold the payload and that the payload decodes with the live game's key (which the case cannot know) to that player, team and game. The Python controller is the reference: these cases describe what it does (controller/tests/test_api_contract.py), and the Android controller must do the same (app/test/controller/api_contract_test.dart).

fixtures.description: Slice S7b of PE24 (presets, mode uploads and signed mode packages, the modes sent to boxes, scenarios, team branding; its cases' names start with 'S7b'): 'values' are saved in every case from the start (a signed mode package of protocol/vectors/mode_package.json, its release text and SHA-256, a 16x16 PNG with a text chunk and the id its checked bytes get, the mode keys). A case may set 'mode_keys' and 'mode_revoked' (the [modes] keys and revoked key ids; none when not given), 'box_keys' (the boxes' mode keys); with slice S7c's 'https' the boxes fetch modes from the address joins carry; scenarios and branding are set up on every controller. A raw request body (S7c's 'body_hex' or 'body_text', with 'mac_key') may name its 'content_type'; an answer's 'headers' (lower-case names) are matched, and one that is not JSON by S7c's 'text' or 'bytes_sha256'. A 'join_decode' also gives 'fetch_modes' and 'forget_modes' (join keys 16 and 17).

field_and_radio.description: Slice S7a of PE24 (decisions PE24-74 to PE24-79): the field plan (field images and floor plans per level, the levels, each plan's map position, the map features with their visibility, the field from a map, the boxes' places) and the field's radio channel with its noise scan, on both controllers. Run after 'cases' with the same rules, and these additions. A request may give 'raw' instead of 'body': {'content_type', 'base64'} sent as the raw body with that Content-Type, zero bytes appended up to 'size' when given (an uploaded image). A request step may check 'content_type' (the answer's media type, without parameters) and 'body_base64' (the answer's bytes); an answer is read as JSON only when it is application/json. Every controller keeps its field plan across a 'restart'. The radio answers each MEASURE (the noise scan) with the noise the case set: a 'noise' step gives, per channel in Hz, [the 90th percentile in dBm, LoRa preambles detected in 10 tries] (a channel not given: -118 dBm and none; the minimum is 6 dB below the 90th percentile, the mean 3, the median 4, the maximum 9 above, the samples as many as the dwell's milliseconds); 'tx' shows each as {'kind': 'measure', 'channel_hz', 'dwell_ms'}. 'hold_measure' makes measurements wait (the scan stays running) and 'scan_wait' lets them go and waits until the scan has ended. A 'tx' step whose 'tx' is '$any' only empties the list.

s7.description: Slice S7 of PE24 (decisions PE24-118 onward): failover (CLAIM, a phone as a Pi's standby or the other way round; ADR-P2-8, PE24-2), and the endpoints of the site sync's schedule, the remote GM's log and the ATAK feed's status without a site server (the sync itself, the remote GM and ATAK are network protocols, tested end to end on each side against a site server and listeners in the tests: controller_sync_test.dart, controller_remote_gm_test.dart, controller_atak_test.dart, and the Pi's test_sync_*.py, test_remote_gm.py, test_atak.py; their bodies against sync.json), on both controllers; its cases' names start with 'S7'. Run after 'field_and_radio' with the same rules, and these additions. A case may set 'failover_mode' ('manual' when not given: the controller's setting for the whole case). An 'rx' step may be another controller's TIME or CLAIM ('time' or 'claim': the payload's fields by name, as for HELLO and STATE); the controller's own CLAIMs are seen by 'tx' steps. A 'join_encode' step seals a join payload with the case's 'join_key' (its fields by protocol/join.md's names, the game key in hex, the region eu868 when not given) and saves its text under 'save' (a standby's join, as the controller that leads makes it). Every controller's priority (ADR-P2-8) is its own (a phone runs on battery), so the cases match it with '$any'.

cases.name: S7 whoami: failover, the schedule and ATAK are served by both controllers; without the site sync
S7 failover: a standby joins from a controller's join, follows its TIME, is promoted and takes over
S7 failover: automatic, the standby claims after three missed beacons, yields to a better claim, keeps its term across a restart
S7 failover: the leading controller steps down to a standby's claim, follows it, and is promoted back

mqtt_acl.description: Who may read and write which topics on the controller's MQTT broker: the Pi's Mosquitto ACL (controller/deploy/atalaia.acl, checked by controller/tests/test_api_contract.py) and the Android controller's embedded broker (app/lib/controller/mqtt_broker.dart, MqttAcl.field, checked by app/test/controller/api_contract_test.dart). Users: 'gm' (GM tools: reads everything, publishes commands), 'reader' (scoreboards: events, score and nodes) and 'controller' (the field controller itself). A user not listed may do nothing.
